articles.title: Paul Elliott backs his power to carry him to shot at ONE Championship MMA heavyweight world title
articles.summary: Paul Elliott headlines ONE Fight Night 48 against unbeaten Shamil Erdogan, with the vacant ONE heavyweight MMA world title potentially within reach; Watch Elliott vs Erdogan on ONE Fight Night 48 live on Sky Sports Mix at 2am on Saturday morning
articles.body:
The Middlesbrough knockout artist could be one victory away from a crack at the vacant ONE heavyweight MMA world championship. A win over undefeated Turkish contender Shamil Erdogan in the main event of ONE Fight Night 48 could punch his ticket to a title shot.

Elliott treats every fight as a reason to be in the best shape of his life, and this one is no different.

"Every single fight I have is motivational because if you don't put yourself in good condition, you're going to get your ass kicked in there. That's without any disrespect to my opponent. He's very good," Elliott said.

Erdogan enters this heavyweight contest with a perfect 13-0 professional MMA record and a 70 per cent finishing rate. The 36-year-old fighter has stopped each of his last eight opponents, and all five of his ONE Championship wins have come by knockout.

Yet for all his power, Erdogan's roots lie on the mat. He took up freestyle wrestling at 12 years old and went on to represent both the Russian and Turkish national teams, even beating former three-division MMA world champion Anatoly Malykhin at a tournament in Russia.

Elliott acknowledges the threat, but he believes the contest will be decided on the feet.

"He's super well-rounded. But I do think his wrestling is better than his striking. Is my striking better than his striking? I believe it is," Elliott said.

"I think I carry more power. I'm definitely more explosive, and I don't think he's fought anyone as explosive as me. I feel like my contractile tissue, my strength, alongside my explosiveness, will help me a lot in this fight."

On current evidence, that is hard to argue with.

The Brit, who owns an 8-2 (1 NC) record, has earned every victory by knockout, seven of them inside the opening minute. The latest came against American college football star Regan Upshaw, whom he dispatched with a head kick and ground punch in just six seconds, tying the fastest knockout in ONE Championship history.

His preparation has been just as serious. Elliott trains at TFT MMA among a who's who of British heavyweight talent, sharing the mats with the likes of UFC star Mick Parkin, KSW Heavyweight Champion Phil De Fries, and Cage Warriors veteran Charles Joyner as he rounds out his game.

"It's a fantastic group of lads," Elliott said. "I believe it's the best heavyweight team in the world. I've got a fantastic room full of heavyweights to train with."

Elliott knows full well the aura of invincibility that surrounds Erdogan. But the Middlesborough native has prepared for this moment, he believes he can live with the Turk's skillset, and he knows that at heavyweight, one shot can change everything.

"He's human. He bleeds. So, there's definitely potential for me to beat him. Can I knock him out? If I land, I know I can knock him out," the Briton said.

"That's definitely in my favour. I know I can knock him out."

Erdogan has spent his career making opponents look ordinary. On Saturday morning, Elliott gets the chance to prove that a perfect record lasts only until someone lands clean - and if he does, a world title shot could be waiting on the other side.

Watch ONE Fight Night 48 live on Sky Sports Mix from 2am on Saturday October 3.

articles.title: Umar Nurmagomedov to make RAF debut against Urijah Faber at Abu Dhabi event days after manager revealed his mindset of quitting wrestling
articles.summary: Umar Nurmagomedov is set to make his Real American Freestyle (RAF) debut against former MMA champion Urijah Faber at RAF Abu Dhabi.
articles.body: Umar Nurmagomedov is set to make his Real American Freestyle (RAF) debut against former MMA champion Urijah Faber at RAF Abu Dhabi. The bout will take place at Etihad Arena on Saturday, November 14. Nurmagomedov is moving to the wrestling mats after competing at the highest level in MMA.The one-time UFC title challenger will face one of the most experienced names in the sport. Faber, known as “The California Kid”, will make his third RAF appearance as he looks for his first win in the promotion.Umar Nurmagomedov faces Urijah Faber in RAF Abu Dhabi debutPromotional officials confirmed that Umar Nurmagomedov has signed with Real American Freestyle and will make his promotional debut against Urijah Faber in Abu Dhabi. The event will take place at Etihad Arena on November 14.Nurmagomedov is making the move to freestyle wrestling after a difficult result in his most recent MMA fight. The 30-year-old suffered a knockout defeat against Song Yadong in the main event of UFC Shanghai in August.Before that loss, Nurmagomedov had returned to winning ways. He defeated Mario Bautista and former UFC flyweight champion Deiveson Figueiredo by decision. Those victories came after his decision loss to then-UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 311 in January 2025.Nurmagomedov has built a strong reputation through his wrestling and grappling skills. The Dagestan native is also part of the famous Nurmagomedov fighting family. He will now take those skills into RAF competition.What makes the move interesting is just a few days ago his manager Ali Abdelaziz revealed a major shift in his mindset. He claimed, “Umar called me the other day, and he was like, ‘I’m not a wrestler. I’m not gonna wrestle again. I’m just gonna knock everybody out. I’m gonna make sure I make it look easy.’”Meanwhile, Faber brings considerably more experience to the wrestling matchup. The former MMA champion and Team Alpha Male founder will make his third appearance for RAF.However, the veteran is still searching for his first victory in the promotion. Faber suffered technical-fall defeats against Henry Cejudo in the main event of RAF 6 in February and Arman Tsarukyan at RAF 8 two months later.The Abu Dhabi card will also feature Kyle Snyder. The reigning RAF light heavyweight champion will face Shamil Erdogan.The inaugural RAF Abu Dhabi event is part of a five-year partnership between Real American Freestyle, the Department of Culture and Tourism - Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi), and the UAE Wrestling Federation.“Abu Dhabi is one of the premier destinations for combat sports, with the vision and infrastructure to deliver events that resonate globally. This five-year partnership gives us the opportunity to make RAF Abu Dhabi a signature event and build something meaningful for athletes, fans and the region for years to come”, Chad Bronstein, CEO and co-founder of RAF, had said earlier.It follows RAF’s international events in Tbilisi, Georgia, and Moscow.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dana White reveals UFC’s role in Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua
articles.summary: After months of waiting, Netflix finally confirmed the much-awaited Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury fight for later this year. The fight is now set to take pla...
articles.body:
After months of waiting, Netflix finally confirmed the much-awaited Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury fight for later this year. The fight is now set to take place on Dec. 11, 2026, at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

UFC president Dana White recently claimed to have a role in promoting the Fury vs. Joshua fight. However, Matchroom Boxing's Eddie Hearn has publicly disagreed about the Zuffa Boxing chief's alleged involvement. Now, White has reacted to his rival's latest remarks.

After missing out on the Fury-Joshua fight press conference, White was recently present on stage when he hosted the UFC 332 press conference in Salt Lake City. There, White was asked to comment on Hearn's statements about White missing the Joshua-Fury press conference despite having a role to play in the fight.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I had the Contender Series (on Tuesday) and I had to be here today," White said. "I fly a lot, but that's a little bit of a rough trip. Not only am I promoting (Fury vs Joshua), we're producing the fight too. UFC is gonna produce the show. I don't know how that's a PR disaster," he added, referencing Hearn's description of the situation," White opened up and addressed his and UFC's role in the fight.

Despite two losses to Oleksandr Usyk and a brief hiatus, Fury came back with two wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach. Fury, 36-2-1, will now enter the boxing ring for the first time against Joshua. Meanwhile, Joshua, 30-4, will fight Fury, having recorded his last two victories over Kristian Prenga and Jake Paul.

articles.title: Denzel Bentley signs with Zuffa Boxing and will fight Shane Mosley Jr at Copper Box Arena on November 7 live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Denzel Bentley will fight Shane Mosley Jr on November 7, live on Sky Sports; Bentley has signed a multi-fight promotional deal with Zuffa Boxing and his clash with Mosley Jr will take place on Zuffa Boxing 12, headlined by Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke
articles.body:
Battersea's Bentley takes on quality American middleweight Shane Mosley Jr on the loaded ZUFFA BOXING 12 bill headlined by Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke.

Tickets are available now via Ticketmaster .

Bentley is a world-class middleweight who became the WBO champion after his tough victory over Endry Saavedra at London's O2 arena in April.

In a hard-fought battle with Saavedra, Bentley came back to take out the dangerous Venezuelan with a strong seventh-round finish.

That saw him win the WBO Interim title which was later upgraded to full world championship.

Bentley has had to battle his way through adversity. A former British champion, he lost his first world title fight when he challenged Zhanibek Alimkhanuly. He then bounced back from a surprise loss to Nathan Heaney, beating Danny Dignum, Derrick Osaze and Brad Pauls to set himself up for the Saavedra bout.

"That's an achievement ticked off, that's one of my goals. I can leave the sport knowing that I was a world champion. But now it's time to try and achieve more and raise my potential. I don't think many people tipped me to be a world champion when I first started," Bentley told Sky Sports .

"I didn't really know if I could even get a chance to compete for one rather than actually win one.

"It's the highest accolade in the sport so you have to do a lot to get there but I just bit down and went through the process and made it there."

Mosley Jr is the son of boxing legend Shane Mosley. He is also coming off an outstanding win in his last fight when he halted strong Ukrainian fighter Serhii Bohachuk in six rounds in Las Vegas.

The American has fought at the highest level, beating former world champion Daniel Jacobs and missing out on the WBC Interim title when he boxed Jesus Alejandro Ramos last year.

British rivals Billam-Smith and Clarke clash in the headline event of ZUFFA BOXING 12 at the Copper Box Arena in London.

London-born cruiserweight prospect Lucas Roehrig, 9-0 (5), will fight Scotland's Connal McDonald, 5-1 (1), in an eight-rounder.

Scottish middleweight phenom Sam Hickey, 6-0 (3), aims for his third consecutive knockout win when he steps up against Troy "The Hawk" Coleman, 15-5-1 (7), in an eight-rounder. Hickey is coming off a scintillating seventh-round stoppage over Brad Axe at Zuffa Boxing 10 in Dublin.

American heavyweight destroyer Da'Mazion Vanhouter, 13-0 (10), makes his UK debut against the big-hitting Ivan Balaz, 9-1 (7) in an eight-rounder. The 21-year-old has six first-round knockouts in his last seven outings.

Super-lightweight star Kayla Allen turned pro last Saturday at Copper Box Arena and her second professional fight will take place in the same venue against an opponent to be named in a six-rounder.

Additional information on the event will be announced in the coming weeks.

While Mosley Jr is not Bentley's mandatory challenger but is ranked No 6 with the WBO.

Bentley told Sky Sports News: "I'm very game. I like to have a fight. I've got a very good knockout ratio, you can expect knockouts. Most importantly I am still currently the WBO middleweight champion.

"I know everything that's gone on online and all the rumours [that he could be stripped of belt]. My team has put in an appeal, that appeal has gone through. We are hoping that we can get through this appeal and we get to defend this WBO title against a game, ranked opponent too.

"The son of a legend, he's there with a chip on his shoulder, trying to prove everyone wrong who believes he can't be as successful as his dad. So he's very dangerous. He's got real motivation and he's going to come in there and put on a great fight."

There will be intriguing possibilities for the Bentley-Mosley Jr victor. Aaron McKenna laid down a marker for the middleweight division when he beat Etinosa Oliha to win the IBF title.

Bentley can consider McKenna a future target, if he comes through his November 7 clash with Mosley Jr.

"I think me and Aaron, the winner of that will be the No 1 in the division," Bentley said.

"If we are the ones making a noise in this division, you can't help make the winner of that fight No 1, rather than looking at [Carlos] Adames or [Erislandy] Lara and looking at their past performances and what they've done in the past and using that to make them No 1.

"We can put the middleweight division back on the map."

Watch Bentley vs Mosley Jr live on Sky Sports on November 7. Tickets for ZUFFA BOXING 12 available now via Ticketmaster .

articles.title: UFC 332: Homeless to history? Bobby Green eyes record-breaking year at 40
articles.summary: At 40 years old, UFC lightweight Bobby Green is showing no signs of slowing down as he sets his sights on a historic end to 2026.
articles.body:
For all that has changed in the UFC over the past 15 years, Bobby Green has remained one of the promotion's few constants.

Green, 40, has racked up more than 30 fights since making his debut in 2013.

Since then, the American has cemented himself as a fan favourite for his all-action and, at times, slightly wild fighting style and his brash personality.

But almost a decade and a half after he first made the walk to the octagon, Green is belatedly enjoying the finest run of his UFC career.

Green is on a four-fight win streak as he prepares to face Esteban Ribovics at UFC 332 in Salt Lake City on Saturday.

He heads into the lightweight bout with a place in the UFC record books in his sights.

After defeating Lance Gibson Jr by split decision last December, Green has recorded stoppage wins over Daniel Zellhuber, Jeremy Stephens and Terrance McKinney.

Victory over Argentina's Ribovics would make it four wins from as many fights in 2026, leaving him one win away from joining an exclusive group of fighters to record five wins in a calendar year. Yet that appears unlikely to satisfy him.

"I get the business and I understand it. There's nothing wrong with that. But I'm not moving," Green said. "I'm not going anywhere. You're going to keep giving me this money."

There are few sports that contrast the bright lights of fight night with the harsh realities of everyday life more starkly than mixed martial arts, and Green has been reminded of that in the build-up to UFC 332.

In September, fewer than six weeks after pocketing a $100,000 (£75,690) Performance of the Night bonus for his knockout of McKinney at UFC 329, Green revealed he was temporarily without a home and was living out of his car.

The situation was met with widespread confusion from the UFC community, including president Dana White, after Green had previously said he had used his career earnings to acquire a number of properties.

Green has since said he had been left without permanent accommodation after all nine of the other properties were occupied by friends, while a break-up with his partner derailed plans to move into another property.

"So about the homeless thing. I am homeless, but I'm not houseless. I can go to anyone's house," Green said on social media.

"I just don't have my home, and I put everybody else before me, just to make sure all my family was taken care of, my friends were taken care of.

"I can go fight and figure it out, but them, it's gonna be harder for them to figure it out."

After a chaotic couple of months for Green, it is little wonder the octagon has felt more like home than ever before.

'The focus is changing my family's life'

Saturday promises to be a pivotal moment that could go some way towards writing the next chapter of Green's storied career.

The veteran is entering the final two fights of his current deal with the UFC and has acknowledged his performance against Ribovics could define what comes next.

After defeating McKinney to match the longest winning streak of his UFC career since 2014 (four fights), Green was keen to be matched against a top-15 opponent in the lightweight division in a bid to reclaim his place in the rankings for the first time since July 2024.

But at 40 years old, Green knows his place in the food chain and accepts he is likely to be used as a yardstick for up-and-coming prospects.

"It's an out-with-the-old, in-with-the-new business," Green said. "Our pay-checks go up, so we've got to get the new guys in to get us guys out of there. Do you know what I mean?

"It's just business. They've got to cut the pay down, keep it to a certain amount. And so if they get rid of some of us guys and make new stars, why not?"

During his media appearances this week, Green made no secret of his dream to one day fight for the symbolic BMF title.

The BMF title is awarded to the 'baddest' fighter in the UFC and has been competed for five times since its inauguration in 2019.

With only a couple of fights left on his deal and currently outside of the rankings, his chances of being matched against the current BMF champion, Charles Oliveira, appear unlikely.

But for someone who has been around the sport long enough to experience his fair share of highs and lows, there is a different dream he is closing in on.

"The focus is changing my family's life and making it a better life," Green said.

"I want to get towards the BMF belt, but at the end of the day, give me my money."

articles.title: Talbott, el psicólogo que se inspira en McGregor para intentar ser campeón de la UFC
articles.standfirst: El peleador estadounidense se medirá a Deiveson Figueiredo en el UFC 332 de este sábado con el objetivo de acercarse al cinturón de peso gallo
articles.summary: El peleador estadounidense se medirá a Deiveson Figueiredo en el UFC 332 de este sábado con el objetivo de acercarse al cinturón de peso gallo
articles.body: El UFC 332 de este sábado ha sido muy criticado por la falta de un evento estelar a la altura, pero la realidad es que la mayoría de combates cumplen con creces las expectativas que genera una cartelera de estas características. Una de las mayores superestrellas del evento será Payton Talbott (11-1), que se enfrentará a todo un ex campeón de peso mosca como Deiveson Figueiredo (25-7-1) para seguir ascendiendo en peso gallo y postularse como un futuro retador al título. Payton desborda carisma, tiene una personalidad muy diferente a la de la mayoría de peleadores y es uno de los mejores strikers de su división. Sin embargo, su sueño de niño no era ser peleador de MMA, hasta que conoció a Conor McGregor y entendió este deporte como un arte. Con 18 años entró al 'Reno Academy of Combat', y curiosamente lo que le hizo engancharse a la disciplina fue la paliza que recibió el primer día, ya que se le olvidaban el resto de problemas que tenía en su vida cotidiana. Mientras evolucionaba como peleador, Talbott se sacó el grado en psicología en Reno, y no fue hasta avanzada su carrera que se decantó por dejar de lado esa faceta. De hecho, siempre tuvo un plan B en la psicología en caso de que las peleas no le diesen los resultados que esperaba. Es más, también fue barista e incluso se planteó ser bombero. Afortunadamente para las MMA, los resultados en su carrera no tardaron en llegar. Sus primeros cinco combates profesionales acabaron en K.O., con algunos de ellos sumando highlights a su historial como el que le propinó a Anthony Jimenez con una rodilla voladora. Inspirado en Conor McGregor, Payton no solo buscaba la victoria, sino convertir su actuación en una forma de expresión muy particular, lo que le permitió recibir la llamada de la UFC para las Dana White's Contender Series. A pesar de que no finalizó su combate, Talbott llamó la actuación de Dana White y se ganó el contrato, y en sus tres primeros combates en la UFC sumó tres finalizaciones que aumentaron el hype sobre su figura. Sin embargo, en enero de 2025 llegó su primera derrota profesional ante Raoni Barcelos, que evidenció sus limitaciones en la pelea en suelo y le dio una valiosa lección que aprovecharía en un futuro. Lejos de venirse abajo, el estadounidense volvió con más fuerza y en los últimos meses ha vencido a dos rivales muy duros como Felipe Lima y Henry Cejudo. Es cierto que ambas victorias han sido por decisión unánime, pero Cejudo es doble campeón de la UFC y medallista de oro olímpico, y aún así estuvo a punto de noquearle y logró derribarle. Por tanto, ha vuelto a ganar enteros para pelear por el cinturón. De hecho, una victoria ante otro ex campeón como Figueiredo le dejaría a una o dos victorias más de la oportunidad, por lo que hay mucho en juego el sábado.

articles.title: Ray Close: Belfast boxing legend dies aged 57
articles.summary: Ray Close, the Belfast boxer who almost handed Chris Eubank the first defeat of his career, has died at the age of 57.
articles.body:
Ray Close, the Belfast boxer who almost handed Chris Eubank the first defeat of his career, has died at the age of 57.

One of the most gifted boxers Northern Ireland has produced, Close was born in 1969 and turned professional in 1988 after a decorated amateur career.

Close won the EBU super-middleweight title on St Patrick's Day in 1993 but it was his bouts against Eubank for which he will be most remembered.

Eubank, who had won all 35 of his professional bouts, was the defending WBO super-middleweight champion in May 1993 but Close pushed him all the way in Glasgow and the pair could not be separated on the scorecards.

A rematch took place at a raucous King's Hall in Belfast the following year and Close put in another strong performance but lost on a split decision.

A third fight was scheduled to take place but Close's boxing licence was revoked by the British Boxing Board of Control before it could take place after a MRI scan revealed two lesions on his brain.

Close would later return to the ring after obtaining a licence in the USA and he won all five of his bouts in Illinois, the last of which was a knockout victory over Larry Willis in June 1997.

His professional record reads as 25 victories, three defeats and one draw - which came against Eubank.

Ledley Hall Youth and Boxing Club in east Belfast, where Close started his boxing journey as a 10-year-old, led tributes and said he was a "true gentleman, humble, kind and always willing to give something back".

"To our young people, Ray was proof of what could be achieved," the club posted on Facebook.

"He was someone who had come through the same doors, trained in the same club and gone on to accomplish incredible things."

The club added that Close's story has "inspired generations of young people at Ledley Hall and will continue to do so".

"There are some people who become part of the history and heart of a place, and Ray will always be part of ours.

"We will remember him with enormous pride, affection and gratitude."

Bangor Abbey Boxing Academy, where Close had trained, said he will be a "huge loss to the boxing fraternity of Ireland and across the world".

"Ray and his whole family have been a huge part of our club over the years, right from the very start and we are truly devastated."

articles.title: ‘Natalia Silva is No. 1 for a reason, but I’m the best striker in the world’: Wang Cong ready for UFC flyweight title moment
articles.summary: Wang Cong has spent much of her fight career moving towards this moment.
articles.body: Wang Cong has spent much of her fight career moving towards this moment. The opponent changed, the timing was short and the rankings may have raised questions, but the objective remained the same. On Saturday, the Chinese fighter gets her chance to become the UFC women's flyweight champion when she takes on No. 1 contender Natalia Silva for the vacant 125-pound title at UFC 332.“Getting the UFC title is reason why I transitioned to MMA. My mind is always there,” Wang told TimesofIndia.com ahead of her main event against Silva.The vacant women's flyweight title became available after Valentina Shevchenko was forced to relinquish the belt because of injury. Silva, the No. 1 contender, had been expected to face Shevchenko and comes into Salt Lake City with an 8-0 UFC record and a 14-fight winning streak. Her last three victories have come against former champions Jessica Andrade, Alexa Grasso and Rose Namajunas.On the other hand, the 34-year-old Wang's route to flyweight title clash has been considerably shorter. She is ranked No. 8 and has six UFC fights behind her, riding on a four-match winnng streak. She most recently beat Tracy Cortez by unanimous decision in July. The ranking difference, however, does not appear to concern her.Silva brings the resume, Wang brings the confidence“No, not at all. I believe I’m the best fighter in the world. I don’t care about rankings,” Wang said, before acknowledging Silva’s credentials.“Yes, she definitely will be the toughest opponent I've ever faced. She’s number 1 for a reason. But I’m the best striker in the world, I believe. So, let’s see on Saturday night.”Silva has built her run around speed, movement, kicks and distance control, while Wang has developed her reputation through accuracy, pressure and power. Wang expects the fight to stay on the feet.“It’s a short notice. I didn’t change too much of my training method. But, I believe this fight will most likely be a stand up fight.”A five-round test and a new challengeShe has also prepared for the first five-round fight of her UFC career and believes her conditioning is sufficient for five rounds.“I think my cardio is always enough for 5 rounds. I definitely did a lot conditioning training for this camp. But it’s more of a mental thing, I believe.”The mental adjustment has been part of Wang's development since the only loss of her professional MMA career. She was submitted by Gabriella Fernandes in November 2024, before responding with four straight decision victories over Bruna Brasil, Ariane da Silva, Eduarda Moura and Cortez.Wang Cong's chance to add another chapter to China's UFC riseThe progression has brought her to a championship fight sooner than many expected. A victory would also give Wang a place in the history of Chinese MMA. Zhang Weili became China's first UFC champion in 2019, while Yan Xiaonan has also challenged for the belt. Wang now has the opportunity to become the country's second UFC champion.“It’s meaningful for myself. From Sanda to kickboxing, to boxing, then to MMA. I always want to accomplish something in every combat sport I compete. And I’m just one step away from my ultimate goal,” she said.Wang also sees the moment as part of a broader rise in Chinese MMA. “It shows China is developing fast in MMA. For women, we have Zhang Weili and Yan Xiaonan. For men, now Song Yadong is the number 3 bantamweight in the world. There will definitely be more to come in the future.”Song, who trains alongside Wang at Team Alpha Male, has also been part of her preparation. He has been giving her advice on both the strategic and mental sides of fighting for a major UFC opportunity and there has been little sign of Wang being overwhelmed by the occasion. Saturday will be her first UFC main event, but she does not regard the setting as fundamentally different.“No, I’ve been competing my whole life. I don’t see this fight as much different.”At Wednesday's media day, Wang tried to encourage Silva to bring more energy to the promotion of the fight, saying she felt both fighters had a responsibility to make the main event a bigger spectacle. Silva has largely kept her attention on the fight itself. She has described winning the UFC title as the goal regardless of who stands opposite her.For Wang, the implications of victory are straightforward. “If I win, it will be the new era of the UFC women's flyweight division. I will be in this spot as long as I can.”Tune-In: Watch UFC 332 - Silva vs. Wang, on Sunday, 4th October 2026, from IST 5.30 AM live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD, Sony Sports Ten 2 SD & HD, Sony Sports Ten 3 SD & HD (Hindi), Sony Sports Ten 4 SD (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada) and Sony LIV.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: CM Punk rebuilt his multimillion-dollar fortune by leaving WWE, conquering UFC, returning to wrestling and turning his unpredictable career into a global brand
articles.summary: Explore how CM Punk transformed his WWE fame into a multimillion-dollar career through UFC, acting, and AEW, culminating in a stunning WWE return.
articles.body: CM Punk, whose real name is Phil Brooks, made his name by bucking wrestling conventions and becoming one of WWE’s most recognizable stars. He left WWE in 2014 after a very successful first run, but his earning potential was not over. Instead, the Chicago-born performer experimented in mixed martial arts, acting and commentary before returning to professional wrestling.Punk’s career is also a demonstration of how a singular personal brand can hold value across a range of entertainment platforms. His wrestling persona translated to UFC promotion, acting, commentary and eventually a return to WWE. Phil Brooks did not follow the traditional linear career path of a single promotion but rather reinvented the CM Punk persona multiple times into new commercial chapters.How CM Punk turned wrestling fame into a multimillion-dollar career beyond WWE through business movesCM Punk’s first big financial base was from his WWE career. Phil Brooks made his name on the independent wrestling circuit and in Ring of Honor before signing with WWE in 2005 and going on to become a multiple-time world champion. A 2011 promo that saw him use a “pipe bomb” got him status as one of the company’s central stars and a 434-day reign as WWE Champion.Punk left WWE in 2014, and then signed with the Ultimate Fighting Championship. His MMA record was thin, but the UFC opportunity showed the commercial value of his existing wrestling profile. Celebrity Net Worth says that his contract reportedly stipulated a flat $500,000 purse to make his UFC debut. MMA Fighting’s expert breakdown had his actual earnings from the fight at $1,042,736, with the added money.He also found time to dabble in acting during his time away from wrestling, with roles in films such as Girl on the Third Floor, Rabid and Jakob’s Wife. Celebrity Net Worth also reports that Punk purchased a home in the Chicago area in 2010 for $2.125 million and a home in Los Feliz, California, in 2021 for $4 million.CM Punk's AEW return reshaped earning power After seven years away from professional wrestling, CM Punk returned with All Elite Wrestling in August 2021. His arrival at The First Dance immediately became one of AEW's most significant moments, bringing a major established wrestling name back into weekly television.Punk subsequently became an AEW World Champion, although injuries and backstage disputes eventually disrupted his run. All Elite Wrestling terminated his contract in 2023, ending another important chapter in his career.The AEW period nevertheless demonstrated that Punk's commercial appeal had survived years away from wrestling. His return generated substantial attention around the promotion and reinforced the value of his name, character and merchandise identity.CM Punk's WWE return strengthened business strategyIn November 2023, CM Punk executed one of the most surprising career reversals in modern wrestling when he returned to WWE at Survivor Series: WarGames. WWE calls the Chicago return a big moment after his dramatic departure in 2014.According to a 2026 report by NDTV, Punk's three-year WWE contract that he signed upon his return was worth an estimated $2.2 million in base salary per year, and with bonuses, merchandise royalties and premium live event fees, his annual compensation could increase to between $3 million and $5 million. These are estimates, not the actual WWE payroll figures that are publicly released.Wealth componentReported or estimated figureEstimated net worth$12 millionWWE estimated base salary$2.2 million annuallyEstimated WWE compensation with additions$3 million- $5 million annuallyChicago property purchase$2.125 millionLos Feliz property purchase$4 millionSo by 2026, his money story is about much more than his wrestling titles. His WWE accomplishments gave him the original platform, the UFC experiment elevated his profile in the public eye, AEW showed that his drawing power still mattered years after his absence, and his return to WWE brought him back to the biggest wrestling company in the world. articles.title: Glover Teixeira says Raoni Barcelos suffered 'traumatic' injury in scary UFC loss: 'Swelling in his brain'
articles.summary: Teixeira cornered Barcelos for his frightening UFC Vegas 121 main-event loss to Raul Rosas Jr. in late September.
articles.body:
One of Raoni Barcelos' cornermen, former UFC light heavyweight champion Glover Teixeira, revealed that Barcelos suffered swelling in his brain stemming from his frightening UFC Vegas 121 main-event loss to Raul Rosas Jr. in late September.

Barcelos, 39, was hospitalized after suddenly losing consciousness during the fifth round of his bantamweight bout against Rosas at the Meta Apex in Las Vegas. Medical personnel immediately entered the cage and Barcelos was eventually carried out on a stretcher. Barcelos was ahead on all three judges' scorecards at the time of the stoppage, and there appeared to be no obvious inciting blow that knocked him out.

Speaking this week on his Portuguese-language "Overdogs" podcast , Teixeira revealed that doctors diagnosed "some swelling in [Barcelos'] brain," leading the Brazilian's team to believe the veteran bantamweight suffered "a traumatic brain injury, and maybe that swelling caused him to black out. It was the body's defense mechanism."

Teixeira's full comments, translation courtesy of MMA Fighting's Guilherme Cruz :

"It was different because it wasn't a knockout. If it had been a knockout, we're used to that. A fighter takes a shot, gets knocked out, OK, let's take him to the hospital, alright. But this was something that happened out of nowhere, and we started thinking about all kinds of things. Could it have been his heart? Could it have been something neurological? They went in and ran the tests. There was some swelling in his brain, so it was a traumatic brain injury, and maybe that swelling caused him to black out. It was the body's defense mechanism. 'Let's shut this down because this guy isn't going to stop.' His mind was stronger than his body, right? He didn't want to give up."

Uncrowned's Ariel Helwani reported in the hours after the event that Barcelos had regained consciousness and was able to speak, and move his fingers and toes. The UFC issued a subsequent confirmation hours later acknowledging that Barcelos was "stable, alert and responsive, with full movement." Barcelos shared an encouraging update this past Monday, stating that he was "doing great;" he was ultimately discharged from the hospital Tuesday night.

The scary ending to UFC Vegas 121's main event cut short an otherwise impressive performance from Barcelos, who appeared to be just minutes away from extending his UFC win streak to six.

Rosas told Uncrowned this week that he initially feared Barcelos had died in the immediate aftermath of the stoppage.

"I was just sitting there, praying," Rosas admitted on "The Ariel Helwani Show." "I did a quick prayer and hoped that he woke up and went back to his family."

Teixeira acknowledged that Barcelos' fighting future remains uncertain, and that the Brazilian requires additional testing before any decisions can be formally made.

"That's going to be a conversation he'll have with his family and everyone else," Teixeira said. "He needs to undergo all the proper tests to find out what happened, whether it really was a result of the trauma from the fight. It's a decision that has to be made with a lot of care and caution."

articles.title: Gautier, de las peleas callejeras en Camerún a superestrella en la UFC
articles.standfirst: 'The Storm' tendrá su primera prueba de fuego en la compañía en el UFC 332 de este sábado ante Roman Kopylov
articles.summary: 'The Storm' tendrá su primera prueba de fuego en la compañía en el UFC 332 de este sábado ante Roman Kopylov
articles.body: Ateba Gautier (11-1) será uno de los nombres más importantes del UFC 332 que se celebrará este sábado en Salt Lake City. El peleador camerunés ha tenido un ascenso meteórico en la división de peso medio, y en esta ocasión tendrá su primera prueba de fuego ante Roman Kopylov (15-5) para demostrar que está preparado para los peces gordos de la categoría. Además, detrás de 'The Storm' hay una increíble historia de superación que merece ser contada. Gautier nació y creció en camerún, donde desde joven estuvo envuelto en peleas callejeras de todo tipo. De hecho, él mismo ha comentado en más de una ocasión que incluso le llegaron a apuñalar con un destornillador, y ni siquiera se dio cuenta hasta que llegó a casa. Tampoco fue al médico, de ahí que su cuerpo esté lleno de cicatrices de esa época. Con tal de salir de las calles se apuntó a un gimnasio con 17 años, y después de un periplo en el sambo dio el salto a las MMA. Apenas dos años después, Carl Prince -entrenador del Manchester Top Team- tuvo la iniciativa de buscar talento emergente en África, descubrió a Ateba y le llevó a Manchester cambiando su vida por completo. En ese momento, Gautier se dio cuenta que podía cambiar la vida de su madre, que había salido adelante con siete hijos haciendo jornadas de hasta 17 horas para poder llevarles a casa un plato caliente. Mientras se iniciaba en su carrera en las MMA estudió física con tal de contentar a su madre, y consiguió cinco victorias en sus seis primeros combates profesionales -cuatro K.O.- para recibir la llamada de la UFC y así poder participar en las Dana White's Contender Series. Gautier noqueó a su rival en el segundo asalto, impresionando a Dana White tanto por el poder de sus manos como por un físico que pocas veces se había visto. Debutó en la UFC en marzo de 2025 con un K.O. por rodillazo en el primer asalto, y desde entonces ha sumado otras cuatro victorias más, tres de ellas por K.O. En 2025 Ateba realizó tres combates, y el que tiene ante Kopylov este sábado también será el tercero de 2026. Un peleador divertido de ver, con poder de K.O. y que compite de manera asidua. Sin duda, una bendición para la compañía. Eso sí, en esta ocasión se medirá al mayor reto de su carrera, ya que Kopylov es otro striker complicado de enfrentar que se ha medido a peleadores de la talla de Paulo Costa, Anthony Hernandez o 'Robocop' Rodrigues. En caso de vencerle daría un golpe sobre la mesa, y si es capaz de noquearlo la UFC se frotaría las manos con el que puede ser el futuro gran nombre de las 185 libras.

articles.title: Umar Nurmagomedov, Urijah Faber added to RAF Abu Dhabi lineup on Nov. 14
articles.summary: Real American Freestyle (RAF) continues to rely heavily on bored UFC fighters looking for side quests, recently adding lightweight contender Umar Nurmagomedo...
articles.body:
Real American Freestyle (RAF) continues to rely heavily on bored UFC fighters looking for side quests , recently adding lightweight contender Umar Nurmagomedov and retired bantamweight bruiser Urijah Faber to its Abu Dhabi lineup, scheduled for Sat., Nov. 14, 2026 at Etihad Arena on FOX Nation.

Nurmagomedov will be making his RAF debut just a couple of months removed from his stunning knockout loss to Song Yadong at UFC Shanghai . As for Faber, who retired from UFC back in late 2019 , he remains winless under the RAF banner following consecutive losses to Henry Cejudo and Arman Tsarukyan .

Elsewhere on the card, reigning RAF Light Heavyweight Champion Kyle Snyder faces the undefeated Shamil Erdogan. In addition, former UFC middleweight champion Khamzat Chimaev battles ex-UFC welterweight title challenger Colby Covington for the RAF Cruiserweight Crossover title in the RAF Abu Dhabi main event.

The inaugural RAF Abu Dhabi card marks the start of a five-year partnership between Real American Freestyle, the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi), and the UAE Wrestling Federation. It follows RAF's international events in Tbilisi, Georgia, and Moscow, Russia, as it continues to build its global professional wrestling platform.

"From day one, our ambition has been to bring RAF to the world's great sports markets, and there is no better place for this next chapter than Abu Dhabi," said Chad Bronstein, CEO and Co-Founder of RAF. "Abu Dhabi is one of the premier destinations for combat sports, with the vision and infrastructure to deliver events that resonate globally. This five-year partnership gives us the opportunity to make RAF Abu Dhabi a signature event and build something meaningful for athletes, fans and the region for years to come."

Additional matchups and further broadcast details will be announced in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Aljamain Sterling says 'hell no' to Jean Silva title shot
articles.summary: Aljamain Sterling doesn't think Jean Silva should leapfrog him as No. 1 contender.
articles.body:
Aljamain Sterling doesn't think Jean Silva should leapfrog him as No. 1 contender.

Sterling (26-5 MMA, 18-5 UFC) called out Silva after the Brazilian scored a third-round submission of Jose Delgado (12-3 MMA, 4-2 UFC) in the UFC Fight Night 288 main event last month.

Silva dismissed Sterling's callout , and is instead targeting the winner of the title fight between Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 on Oct. 24.

"He had a great win – well, finish," Sterling said of Silva on "The Ariel Helwani Show." "It was a tough performance against a guy who stepped up on short notice – tall, rangy, young kid, as well. He was calling for a title shot, and I think he might think I have bad blood against him. No dude. We're trying to do the same thing here. So if you think you're next and I think I'm next, let's figure it out. It's nothing bigger than that."

Sterling, who snapped Youssef Zalal's win streak in the UFC Fight Night 274 main event , drew red-hot contender Kevin Vallejos (18-1 MMA, 4-0 UFC) at UFC Fight Night 294 on Nov. 21 at ABHA Arena in Doha ( Paramount+ ). He disagrees with Silva getting the next title shot.

"Hell no," Sterling said. "He better fight someone else. What I honestly think it's going to come down to is who looks the best these next coming months, and then who wins the title fight between Movsar and the champ, Volkanovski."
